title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a proof begun on p.87 (archive p.90): Lemma 1 / Prop. 3 on 'transpositions' between two sets E, E' that each carry a support or saturation operator. The underlying data appear to be as follows.
- A support operator on each set: sup_{W°_E}, written s-W°_E or s-Ψ°_E in the transcription; next page also writes sat_W.
- A family Σ_E of 'supported' (saturated) subsets.
- A symmetric relation A |∘| B on subsets, best read as 'A meets B'.
- Multivalued maps α: E → P(E') and β: E' → P(E), extended to subsets as ᾱ and β̄.
- They are 'transposed' when x |∘| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |∘| x'. For pointwise maps this just says β is the relation-transpose of α.

On p.87 two steps were done. (i) ⇔ (ii) is the extension from points to subsets. The key observation is that both sides of the |∘| relations are unchanged when a term is replaced by its support. This is the familiar fact that A meets an open U iff the closure of A meets U.

This page proves (iii) ⇒ (ii).
- Rewriting (b): replacing every term by its support gives sup(A) |∘| sup(β̄(A')) ⇔ sup(ᾱ(A)) |∘| sup(A').
- Formulas (c), with Ā, Ā' the supports of A, A', state that sup(β̄(A')) = sup(β̄(Ā')), defined as β_*(Ā'). Likewise sup(ᾱ(A)) = sup(ᾱ(Ā)), defined as α_*(Ā).
- Hence Ā |∘| β_*(Ā') ⇔ α_*(Ā) |∘| Ā'. This is the transposition condition (iii) between the induced maps α_*: Σ_E → Σ_{E'} and β_*: Σ_{E'} → Σ_E.

Grothendieck notes that it remains to justify the two equalities (c), and by symmetry only the second.

Corollary: under Lemma 1, for any A ⊂ E with Ā = sup(A), one has sup(ᾱ(A)) = sup(ᾱ(Ā)).
- Proof of ⊂: A ⊂ Ā gives ᾱ(A) ⊂ ᾱ(Ā), and the support is monotone.
- Proof of ⊃: supports are tested against members of Σ, so it suffices to show, for all A' ∈ Σ_{E'}, that A' |∘| ᾱ(A) ⇔ A' |∘| ᾱ(Ā).
- Next page finishes this: transposing turns both sides into β_*(A') |∘| A and β_*(A') |∘| Ā, which are equivalent by the support invariance.

Consequence (p.89):
- α_*(sup x) = sup α(x) =: α'(x).
- α_*(S) = sup_{x∈S} α'(x).
- So the induced map on supported sets depends only on α', the composite of α with sup.

In modern terms: a relation compatible with closure-type operators induces a pair of mutually 'adjoint' (meet-transposed) maps between the lattices of closed or saturated sets. This is a Galois-connection / closure-system lemma, comparable to lower semicontinuity of multivalued maps or the functoriality of relations between closure spaces. The page serves the foundational part of the 'Ateliers' chapter: passing from point-level relations to maps between lattices of supports.
errors: The ⊃ step of the corollary is reduced to testing intersections with all A' ∈ Σ_{E'}. This tacitly uses that a support is determined by which elements of Σ it meets: Σ must 'separate' supports, as open sets do for closures. This hypothesis is presumably among the standing assumptions but is not restated here.

The equalities (c) are first used, then flagged as still needing proof, then proved as a corollary. The logical order on the page is loose but not wrong, since the corollary does not depend on (iii) ⇒ (ii).
Some crossed-out false starts (e.g. 'Si nous prouvons que s-Ψ(β̄(A')) = s-Ψ_E ...') show the argument being restructured; there is no substantive error.

ideas.what: Transposed multivalued maps α: E→P(E'), β: E'→P(E) with α(x) meets x' iff x meets β(x'), extended to subsets
ideas.modern_name: relation and its converse; Galois connection between power sets

ideas.what: Invariance of 'A meets B' under replacing a term by its support/saturation, used to pass the transposition condition to saturated sets
ideas.modern_name: closure operators / closure systems; the fact that A meets an open U iff cl(A) meets U

ideas.what: Induced maps α_*, β_* on lattices of supported sets, with α_*(S) = sup_{x∈S} α'(x) and α_* depending only on α' = sup∘α
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of join-preserving maps between closure lattices (sup-lattice morphisms induced by relations)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine lattice/closure-operator bookkeeping inside a longer proof. The results are elementary and standard; only the context (the 1986 'Ateliers' chapter) is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: The operator written 's-Ψ°_E' is in the image 's—W°_E', i.e. the same 'sup_{W°_E}' (support with respect to W°_E) that the next page writes explicitly. Ψ is a misreading.
In (c) the bracketed definitions read '(=^{déf} β_*(Ā'))' and '(=^{déf} α_*(Ā))', as transcribed, with the def sign over '='.

'on en conclut que ces équivalences...' is better read as 'on en conclut que (b) s'écrit aussi', followed by the displayed equivalence Ā|∘|β_*(Ā') ⇔ α_*(Ā)|∘|Ā', then 'ce qui n'est autre que (iii)/(ii)'.
After '//' read roughly: 'Donc il reste à prouver (en vertu de (ii) indiqués) les deux relations (c) — et il suffit (par raison de symétrie) de prouver la seconde :'.
Corollary: 'Sous les conditions du lemme 1 (cas (ii)), si A ∈ P(E), A' ∈ P(E'), Ā = sup_{W°_E}(A), Ā' = sup_{W°_{E'}}(A'), on a les relations (c) ci-dessus.' The final reference is to (c), not (ii).
The last line is 'il faut prouver ⊃. Il revient au même de dire que ∀A' ∈ Σ_{E'}, on a A'|∘|ᾱ(A) ⇔ A'|∘|ᾱ(Ā)', with the sup symbols and the alternative 'α_*(Ā)' crossed out.
